01.event: In a case before him, Rabbi ruled (or meant to rule) according to the Rabbis of the mishna, and Perata objected that this would leave the court no more power than an ordinary person.
01.outcome: Rabbi reversed his ruling (in Rav Safra's version, he never carried it out).
01.summary: Rav Dimi reported a case in which Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi ruled according to the Rabbis of the mishna. Perata, grandson of Rabbi Perata the Great, objected that if so, the court would have no more power than an ordinary person. Rabbi then reversed his ruling. Rav Safra told it slightly differently: Rabbi only wanted to rule that way, and after the objection he did not do it.

02.event: A yavam and yevama who both said they had not consummated the levirate marriage came before Rava, and he ordered halitza for her.
02.turn: Rav Sherevya cited a baraita requiring both a bill of divorce and halitza.
02.outcome: Rava accepted it and retracted his ruling.
02.summary: A yavam and his yevama came before Rava, both saying they had never consummated the levirate marriage. Rava told the scholars to arrange halitza for her and settle her case. Rav Sherevya objected that a baraita requires both a bill of divorce and halitza. Rava answered that if the baraita teaches it, so be it, and withdrew his ruling.

04.event: Rabban Gamliel's daughter was married to his brother Abba, who died childless, and Rabban Gamliel then took her rival wife in levirate marriage.
04.summary: Rabban Gamliel's daughter was married to his brother Abba. Abba died without children, and Rabban Gamliel took his daughter's rival wife in levirate marriage. The Gemara cites this as an incident, but only as evidence in a legal argument; no turn or ending follows.
04.missing: Any turn or consequence of the incident; the text only reports the act.

05.event: Doubting a ruling Rav Beruna attributed to Shmuel, Rabbi Elazar had Rav Beruna show him Shmuel's lodging and asked Shmuel directly, who confirmed it.
05.turn: Rabbi Elazar challenged Shmuel with Shmuel's own earlier statement that contradicted the ruling.
05.outcome: Shmuel was silent and did not answer.
05.summary: Rav Beruna was reciting a ruling of Shmuel. Rabbi Elazar doubted Shmuel had said it, so he asked to be shown Shmuel's lodging and went to ask him himself. Shmuel confirmed it. Rabbi Elazar then pointed to another statement of Shmuel's that seemed to contradict it, and Shmuel fell silent.

07.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi (and the people of Bireta DeSatya)
07.event: On his deathbed Rabbi made prophetic statements about places in Babylonia, including that the people of Bireta DeSatya had that day turned away from God.
07.turn: They had trapped fish on Shabbat when a ditch overflowed, and Rabbi Ahai excommunicated them.
07.outcome: They all became apostates; Rabbi also announced that Adda bar Ahava was circumcised that day and Rav Yehuda was born.
07.summary: As Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi lay dying, he made prophetic pronouncements about Babylonian places, such as towns whose people were Ammonites or mamzerim. He said that on that day the people of Bireta DeSatya had turned from God: a fish ditch overflowed and they caught the fish on Shabbat, Rabbi Ahai excommunicated them, and they all abandoned Judaism. He added that Adda bar Ahava of Akra DeAgma was being circumcised that day and that Rav Yehuda had just been born.

08.event: On three questions of double liability, Rabbi Hiyya and Bar Kappara each jumped up and swore by the Temple service that he had heard his opposite ruling from Rabbi, then each argued his case.
08.summary: Rabbi Hiyya and Bar Kappara disagreed over whether someone who breaks two prohibitions in one act is liable twice or once. Three times, each jumped up and swore by the Temple service that he had heard his own ruling from Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, and each then argued his reasoning. The scene of the competing oaths is vivid, but it never resolves. What follows is the Gemara's legal analysis.
08.missing: A resolution of the confrontation; the text moves into legal analysis.

09.event: Ten men carried a woman out on a bier, as if she were dead, and had intercourse with her.
09.summary: Rav ruled that a woman may not be secluded even with ten immoral men, and an incident is cited as proof. Ten men carried a woman out on a bier as if she were dead and had intercourse with her. The report is a single bare line given as evidence for the ruling.
09.missing: Who was involved and any aftermath; the incident is told in one line.

12.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a certain ruling, and his student Abaye reminded him that he had taught it to them himself.
12.turn: It is revealed that Rav Yosef had forgotten his own teaching.
12.summary: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a certain ruling. His student Abaye told him that he himself had taught it to them, and said where he had taught it. The passage does not say how Rav Yosef responded.
12.missing: Rav Yosef's reaction; the explanation that his illness made him forget comes only from the translator's gloss.

13.event: Rav Safra raised objections to a ruling Abaye was reciting in Rav Yosef's name, and Abaye could not answer.
13.turn: Abaye reported the objections to Rav Yosef.
13.outcome: Rav Yosef told him the answer he should have given: members of a Paschal group are vigilant.
13.summary: Abaye was teaching a ruling of Rav Yosef when Rav Safra challenged it with mishnayot. Abaye deflected the first challenge but could not answer the second and fell silent. He went to Rav Yosef and told him what Rav Safra had said. Rav Yosef asked why he had not answered that members of a Paschal lamb group are vigilant.

14.actor: A man and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya
14.event: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags, and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya examined it before Rav to see whether it was worth a peruta.
14.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags. Sitting before Rav, Rav Shimi bar Hiyya examined the bundle to see whether it was worth a peruta, which would decide whether the betrothal was valid. The text does not say what he found, and the Gemara moves on to a legal question.

15.event: Rabbi Eliezer missed the study hall, met Rabbi Asi, and asked him what had been said there.
15.turn: Rabbi Asi told him Rabbi Yohanan ruled like Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Eliezer asked whether that meant only one authority disagreed.
15.outcome: Rabbi Asi said yes and cited a baraita.
15.summary: One day Rabbi Eliezer did not go to the study hall. He met Rabbi Asi and asked what had been said there. Rabbi Asi said Rabbi Yohanan had ruled according to Rabbi Yosei. Rabbi Eliezer asked whether only a single authority disagreed, and Rabbi Asi confirmed it with a baraita. It is a frame for a legal exchange rather than a full story.

16.actor: Rava and Rav Natan bar Ami
16.event: Rava compelled the wealthy Rav Natan bar Ami to give charity and collected four hundred dinars from him.
16.outcome: Four hundred dinars were collected for charity.
16.summary: To show that a court may compel a wealthy man, the Gemara cites a case: Rava forced the wealthy Rav Natan bar Ami to give charity and took four hundred dinars from him. The case is told in a single line as a precedent.
16.missing: Any background or reaction; the case is a bare precedent.

17.actor: Rav Avya and his wife, the sister of Rami bar Hama
17.event: When the couple's marriage contract was lost, they came before Rav Yosef, who first said they could continue without one for a while.
17.turn: Abaye objected that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's decrees.
17.outcome: Rav Yosef told Rav Avya to go and write her a new marriage contract.
17.summary: Rami bar Hama's sister was married to Rav Avya, and her marriage contract was lost. They asked Rav Yosef, who said the strict view was Rabbi Meir's, while the Rabbis allow a man to stay with his wife for two or three years without one. Abaye objected that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees. Rav Yosef then told Rav Avya to go and write her a new contract.

18.event: At his son Abba Mar's wedding, Rav Pappa poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda.
18.turn: Rav Yitzhak did not stand up for him.
18.summary: Rav Pappa was serving drinks to the guests at his son Abba Mar's wedding. When he poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda, Rav Yitzhak did not stand for him, and Rav Pappa was offended. The Gemara concludes that even when a rabbi forgoes his honor, some gesture of respect is still required.

19.event: When Rabbi Elazar moved to Eretz Yisrael, was ordained, and joined the council for intercalating the calendar, he each time declared that he had escaped another curse.
19.turn: Each step freed him from one of the three curses in Ezekiel on false prophets.
19.outcome: He had escaped all three curses.
19.summary: When Rabbi Elazar went up to Eretz Yisrael, he said he had been spared one curse. When he was ordained, he said he had been spared two, and when he was seated on the council that intercalated the calendar, he said three. The three were Ezekiel's curses on false prophets: shut out of the council, the register of Israel, and the land of Israel.

20.event: Rav Yosef taught a ruling in the name of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, and Rav Beivai told the Sages not to listen to him.
20.turn: Rav Beivai said he had given Rav Yosef the teaching himself, in Rav Adda bar Ahava's name, and that it was about 'many', not 'Rabbi'.
20.outcome: Rav Yosef exclaimed 'Master of Abraham!' and admitted he had confused 'rabbim' with 'Rabbi'.
20.summary: Rav Yosef taught a ruling about courtyards in the name of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. Rav Beivai told the Sages not to listen: he had taught it to Rav Yosef himself, in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava, and it concerned the word 'many' (rabbim). Rav Yosef exclaimed 'Master of Abraham!' and admitted he had confused 'rabbim' with 'Rabbi'.
